cards.explanation: The answer is Golgotha. John says the Place of the Skull "…in Hebrew is called Golgotha." It's a name that sticks with you, friends.
The answer is True. John says two others are crucified with Jesus, "…one on each side, with Jesus in the middle." Jesus is the one in the center. John tells us exactly where everyone stands.

The answer is The King of the Jews. The notice reads: "JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS." Pilate, the Roman governor, is the one who had it posted. Right there on the cross, in plain letters, friends.
The answer is city. John says "…the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city…" That's why "Many of the Jews…" read the sign. Being near the city is the reason John gives.

The answer is that they want it to say only that He said He was the king. The chief priests tell Pilate: "Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’…" See the little shift, bakers? They want the sign to say He claimed it, instead of stating it as the title.

The answer is False, and you can hear it in Pilate's own words. He answers, "What I have written, I have written." The chief priests asked for a change, and he didn't give in. The sign stays as he wrote it.

The answer is that they cast lots to see who gets it. The soldiers say to one another, "Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it." The tunic is "…seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom," so cutting it up would ruin it. Four soldiers, one tunic, and they settle it by lots.

The answer is Scripture. John says it happened "…to fulfill the Scripture…" and then he quotes: "They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing." A similar line is in Psalm 22:18. It's a verse you can find in your own Bible, friends.
The answer is True. John says, "Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother and her sister…" Mary the wife of Clopas and Mary Magdalene are there too. John lists the people standing close.

The answer is "Woman, here is your son." Jesus says it to His mother as He sees her and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby. John writes down those exact words, and I think they carry a lot in a few syllables, friends.
The answer is mother. Jesus says to the disciple, "Here is your mother." The words mirror what He just told His mother, "Woman, here is your son." It's one whole exchange, friends.
The answer is True. John says, "…from that hour, this disciple took her into his home." Jesus said the words, and the disciple acted on them right away. John doesn't hold anything back.

The answer is on a sponge on a stalk of hyssop. John says they "…soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth." The jar of sour wine was already sitting there. The sponge and the hyssop stalk are the detail John gives.

The answer is "It is finished." John writes, "When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit." That's a heavy part, friends, so I'll let John's own words stand.
